title: Structured Coupling for Flow Matching
claim: Standard methods transport from an unstructured fixed source; ours learns a structured source jointly with transport via a shared network.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, left-to-right flow, colored latent clusters in right panel
description: Two rounded panels are placed side by side. The left, gray panel is titled 'FM (Standard Flow Matching)'. It shows a fixed Gaussian source cloud x0 ~ N(0,I) labeled unstructured. A t=0 to t=1 interpolant with a flow-matching velocity arrow leads to a column of four generated images: a dog, a lake, a cat and a hummingbird. The right, green panel is titled 'SCFM (Structured Coupling Flow Matching)'. Data images enter a purple 'Shared Network' box. It produces latent clusters in blue, red and green, labeled as a learnable structured prior. These clusters feed the augmented source x0=(z,ε) and the flow-matching timeline. A teal decoder box handles reconstruction. The output images carry colored borders that match the clusters. Equations sit above each stage, and a legend runs along the bottom. The eye goes first to the colorful scatter clusters in the center.
caption: While standard flow matching (left) relies on a fixed, unstructured source, SCFM (right) replaces this with an augmented source x0 = (z, ε). An encoder induces a data-dependent coupling, distilling semantic structure into a learnable prior (indicated by colored latent clusters). Crucially, a single shared network serves as both the endpoint variational encoder for prior learning and the intermediate-time posterior estimator for flow velocity. This unified objective yields a structured latent space without sacrificing the continuous, simulation-free transport of standard flow models.
abstract: Standard flow matching scales well but typically relies on an unstructured source distribution, limiting its ability to learn interpretable latent structure. Latent-variable models, by contrast, capture structure but often sacrifice generative quality. We bridge this gap by proposing Structured Coupling for Flow Matching (SCFM), a cooperative framework that augments flow matching with structured latent representation learning. By introducing structured latent variables and exogenous noise into the source, SCFM jointly learns a structured prior (via latent variable modeling) and a continuous transport map (via flow matching). It uses a shared time-dependent recognition network for both latent variable model variational inference and intermediate-time flow velocity estimation. This yields a structurally informed yet unconditional, simulation-free flow model, where the latent variable model can also assist flow sampling. Empirically, SCFM facilitates unsupervised latent representation learning for clustering, disentanglement and downstream tasks, while remaining competitive with flow matching in sample quality, showing that meaningful structure can be learned without sacrificing generative fidelity.
